title: CrFeVW<i>X</i> (<i>X</i> = Ta or Ti) High-Entropy Alloy: A Theoretical and Experimental Comparative Investigation on Phase Stability.

recollection.starting_material: Guess: equiatomic mixtures of elemental Cr, Fe, V, W, and X (Ta or Ti) powders
recollection.intervention: Guess: arc-melting followed by homogenization anneal and controlled cooling
recollection.structure: Guess: predominantly BCC solid solution for X=Ta; mixed BCC and ordered Laves or B2 phases for X=Ti
recollection.mechanism: Guess: high configurational entropy stabilizes single-phase BCC with Ta; Ti’s larger size mismatch and negative enthalpy interactions drive secondary phase precipitation
recollection.results: Guess: Ta-containing alloy shows a single-phase BCC with hardness ~350 HV and yield strength ~1.2 GPa; Ti-containing alloy exhibits two-phase microstructure with hardness ~400 HV and yield strength ~1.4 GPa

score.note: The starting elemental mixture is correctly guessed, but the processing route is wrong: the study used MD/MC simulations, mechanical alloying, and spark plasma sintering rather than arc melting and annealing. The recollection generically identifies bcc-related structures, but reverses the secondary-phase behavior: Fe2Ta Laves formed in the Ta alloy, while the Ti alloy showed two bcc-type phases. The proposed size-mismatch mechanism is incorrect because Ta and Ti have similar radii, and the quantitative hardness and strength values were not reported; the actual quantitative results concerned lattice parameters, density, segregation temperatures, and thermal diffusivity.
